title: Lines, characters and jumps
summary: Jump within a line with 0 ^ $ f t ; , and across the file with gg G :n % { }.

steps.title: Within a line
body: | `f` + char | next occurrence of that char on the line |
| `,` | repeat it in the opposite direction |
`f` is the fastest way to reach a spot you can see: look at the character, type `f` and it.
> **Practise:** open **Labs → Vim & nano trainer** and run this lesson's challenges until the keys come without thinking.

steps.prompt: The line is `    return x + y;` (four leading spaces) and the cursor is on the `x`. You press `^`. Which character is the cursor on?
steps.explain: `^` goes to the first non-blank character; `0` would go to the very first column (a space).

steps.prompt: The line is `a,b,c,d` with the cursor on `a`. You press `f,` then `;` then `;`. Which letter comes right after the cursor's comma?
steps.explain: `f,` reaches the first comma, each `;` the next: three commas in, the cursor is on the comma before `d`.

steps.prompt: The line is `name = "value"` with the cursor on `n`. Which keys put the cursor on the `e` that ends `value`?
steps.explain: `$` reaches the closing quote and `h` steps back one. Three `e`s stop at `name`, `=`, then the opening quote; two `f"` land on the closing quote.

steps.title: Across the file
body: | `H` `M` `L` | top / middle / bottom of the screen |
| `Ctrl+O` | back to where you were before the last jump |
`%` is a lifesaver in code and JSON: put the cursor on a brace and jump to its partner. If the cursor is not on a bracket, `%` uses the first one to the right on the line.

steps.prompt: Match the keys to the jump.
Go to the first line, then jump to the brace that matches the one at the end of that line.
steps.explain: `gg` first line, `$` to its last character (the `{`), `%` to the matching `}`.

steps.title: Match the bracket
prompt: Write `int Percent(string line, int col)` modelling `%` on one line:
- find the first bracket among `()[]{}` at or after `col`; if there is none, return `col`.
- jump to its match, counting nesting of the **same** bracket type (`(` and `)` only count each other). Opening brackets search right, closing ones search left.
- if there is no match, return `col`.
solution: for (int i = col; i < line.Length; i++)
for (int i = start; i >= 0 && i < line.Length; i += step)
else if (line[i] == partner) { depth--; if (depth == 0) return i; }
hints: First scan right for any bracket.
Then walk in its direction with a depth counter: same char +1, partner -1, stop at 0.
template: Dojo.Eq("from before the first bracket", 9, Percent("f(a, g(b))", 0));
